newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bunds remain down but seen resilient.
newsitem.headline: Bunds remain down but seen resilient.

text.p: German Bunds remained weak in late trade after slipping at the open on an overnight decline in U.S. Treasuries but dealers said the German market was well supported and some predicted slight gains on Friday.

June Bund futures were quoted down 0.38 points at 101.44 at 1555 GMT after having traded in a range of 101.37 to 101.62 during the session. Dealers said the contract had technical support at 101.25 and 100.90.
Dealers said trading was dominated by technical factors with little investor interest in the cash Bund market.
The yield on the 10-year benchmark six percent government bond was 5.71 percent up from 5.67 percent late on Wednesday.

Dealers were impressed by the resilience of the Bund market in the face of a drop in Treasuries on Thursday following news that U.S. retail sales rose a brisk 0.8 percent in February, above forecasts for a 0.6 percent rise.
The January increase in retail sales was revised up strongly to 1.5 percent, the strongest surge in nearly a year.
"We're holding up really well against Treasuries," one Frankfurt-based Bund dealer said.
"I'm still positive for this market and I think Bund futures might even test 102.00 tomorrow."
But he added that trading was likely to be rangebound during Friday morning ahead of the release at 1330 GMT of U.S. producer prices for February.
